title: Cabin front study: coherent adjacent seats
beat: Establish two forward-facing seat assemblies for later chapter continuity.
camera: From front windshield/dashboard looking rearward,35mm perspective.
staging: Beaver image-left in suspended driver chair, PinPin image-right in compact inner-fender bracket-mounted buddy seat.
alt: Front-facing study of Beaver at steering and PinPin beside him in a compact forward-facing instructional seat.

references.role: Primary manufacturer geometry reference only; compact bracket-mounted instructional seat beside full suspended operator seat.
Only established character identity, proportions, blue vest, red cab/gray materials; NOT seating geometry or camera.
Only front-view physical side mapping: Beaver image-left and PinPin image-right; exterior tractor identity.

prompt:
Use case: illustration-story and precise-object-edit. Create ONE NEW coherent cabin-layout STUDY for this established red storybook tractor, landscape1536x1024. This is a new camera composition, not a pixel-preserving edit. Polished warm dimensional woodland children's-book rendering.
REFERENCE ROLES: Image1 is a real manufacturer photograph: use ONLY its geometric distinction between one large suspended tractor operator seat and one compact thin-cushion, low-back folding instructional/buddy seat attached to the adjacent inner fender/cab structure. Do not copy its beige fabric or green paint. Image2 is ONLY Beaver/PinPin character identity, relative animal size, blue vest, and red-cab/gray-material rendering; discard its old passenger-chair geometry and old camera. Image3 is ONLY established FRONT VIEW side mapping and red tractor identity: Beaver on IMAGE LEFT, PinPin on IMAGE RIGHT.
CAMERA: Look from the FRONT windshield/dashboard BACK into the cab, at seated-animal eye height, modest wide35mm perspective without fisheye. Both animals, both seat cushions, both backrests and their two distinct mounting arrangements are clearly visible in one believable compact cab. The single steering wheel is in the near foreground on IMAGE LEFT, ahead of Beaver. Forest and subtle empty trailer/headboard hints may be visible through REAR glazing behind them. Never put the tractor bonnet or forward road in the rear window. Red structural cab pillars, gray interior, rubber floor, real-looking tractor controls. Keep the shot intimate enough to show seat construction, without excessive empty cab space.
FIXED PHYSICAL LAYOUT: Two adjacent seats facing the tractor's front/camera in PARALLEL, in the SAME seating row. Main driver seat central/slightly machine-RIGHT = IMAGE LEFT in this front camera. Compact passenger seat on machine-LEFT = IMAGE RIGHT, beside the operator, mounted against the machine-left inner fender/cab-side structure. Seat front edges and both animals' seated pelvis/body axes face the camera. Neither seat points across the aisle at the other animal, nor toward the side door. Do not mirror this mapping.
BEAVER: established warm chestnut beaver from Image2, blue work vest, broad whiskered muzzle, two modest incisors and small round ears. Seated naturally IMAGE LEFT in one full-size dark-gray operator seat with one upright padded seatback BEHIND his body, one cushion UNDER hips/thighs and one normal black suspension unit underneath. Both forepaws hold the SINGLE steering wheel in front of him; two hind paws align toward floor controls. His lap belt lies low across seated hips, visibly anchored at two seat sides. Driver seating, wheel and pedals form one fore-aft axis. Tractor-style modest operator arm supports only if needed, not a furniture lounge chair.
PINPIN: established small cream-faced hedgehog from Image2 with expressive dark eyes, pointed brown quills and no clothing. IMAGE RIGHT on a genuinely COMPACT instructional/buddy seat: one shallow dark-gray cushion beneath seated hips and paws, ONE low backrest BEHIND his torso/quills, both on ONE SHORT visible folding/bracket mount fixed to the inner left fender/cab structure. This is a species-sized adaptation of the manufacturer buddy seat, not a second freestanding driver chair. No tall box, pedestal, suspension bellows, giant booster, lounge armrests or duplicate backrest. Cushion is a small fraction of driver cushion size but supports him comfortably. Cushion front edge points toward camera; rear backrest is behind him, never between him and camera. His body faces camera/tractor front; head may turn slightly toward Beaver. His forepaws rest naturally on the cushion/front of his body; visible lower-body contact establishes seated support. A modest lap belt lies across hips, anchored on BOTH sides to this compact seat/bracket structure with one small side buckle; never across throat, floating, wrapped around quills or attached to door/dashboard. One small appropriate foot support may be part of the SAME compact bracket, no separate stool.
Show precisely TWO seat assemblies and TWO animals. Keep main seat and compact buddy seat adjacent without crowding bodies, steering or door. Preserve recognisable character faces and relative size; reposition bodies and build realistic cabin architecture as needed to demonstrate this coherent physical layout. This is a visual continuity study, not an engineering certification. No additional passenger, no bench, no opposing chairs, no second steering wheel, no duplicated cushion/backrest/base, no labels, no arrows, no text or brand logos, no collage.
review: Front windshield camera and physical side mapping are coherent: Beaver image-left at the sole steering wheel and PinPin image-right. Both seat cushions and seated bodies face forward, with one seatback behind each animal. Driver has one suspension base; PinPin seat has a compact visible side bracket and no freestanding pedestal or bellows. Both forepaws hold the wheel; PinPin has no steering wheel. Lap belts cross low body areas with visible side buckles. Caveats: PinPin backrest remains larger/taller and cushion thicker than the compact shallow manufacturer reference; bracket-to-fixed-cab versus moving-door structure is not fully unambiguous; both belt anchor endpoints are not fully visible, so attachment correctness cannot be certified. Beaver hind paws rest near cushion/base instead of clearly reaching pedals. Unrequested LOADED LOGS appear through rear glazing, conflicting with intended pre-loading/empty trailer story state. No hood/forward road appears through rear glass. Character identity broadly retained, but this new study redraws faces and must receive user approval. Useful for layout review, NOT a chapter-ready scene05 replacement or engineering certification. No automatic iteration or publication.
